signature: SUBROUTINE DSYGVX( ITYPE, JOBZ, RANGE, UPLO, N, A, LDA, B, LDB,

params.name: itype
params.reference:
Specifies the problem type to be solved:

-   `= 1`: $A \, x = (\lambda ) \, B \, x$
-   `= 2`: $A \, B \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$
-   `= 3`: $B \, A \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$

params.name: jobz
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
-   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

params.name: range
params.reference:
-   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found.
-   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found.
-   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.

params.name: uplo
params.reference:
-   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A and B are stored;
-   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A and B are stored.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix pencil (A,B). $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference:
On entry, the symmetric matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A.

On exit, the lower triangle (if `UPLO='L'`) or the upper triangle (if `UPLO='U'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed.

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: B
params.reference:
On entry, the symmetric matrix B. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of B contains the upper triangular part of the matrix B. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of B contains the lower triangular part of the matrix B.

On exit, if $\mathrm{INFO} \le N$, the part of B containing the matrix is overwritten by the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $B = U^T \, U$ or $B = L \, L^T$.

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: vl
params.reference: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.

params.name: vu
params.reference: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.

params.name: il
params.reference: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.

params.name: iu
params.reference: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.

params.name: abstol
params.reference:
The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

$$
\mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
$$

where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing C to tridiagonal form, where C is the symmetric matrix of the standard symmetric problem to which the generalized problem is transformed.

Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

params.name: m
params.reference: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.

params.name: w
params.reference: On normal exit, the first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.

params.name: Z
params.reference:
If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. The eigenvectors are normalized as follows: if `ITYPE = 1` or 2, $Z^T \, B \, Z = I$; if `ITYPE = 3`, $Z^T \, \operatorname{inv}(B) \, Z = I$.

If an eigenvector fails to converge, then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.

params.name: ldz
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Z. $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge 1$, and if `JOBZ = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The length of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,8 \, N)$. For optimal efficiency, $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge (\mathrm{NB}+3) \, N$, where NB is the blocksize for DSYTRD returned by ILAENV.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: IFAIL
params.reference: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: DPOTRF or DSYEVX returned an error code: \<= N:  if `INFO = i`, DSYEVX failed to converge; i eigenvectors failed to converge.  Their indices are stored in array `IFAIL`.
-   `> N`: if $\mathrm{INFO} = N + i$, for $1 \le i \le N$, then the leading principal minor of order i of B is not positive. The factorization of B could not be completed and no eigenvalues or eigenvectors were computed.

checks.js: range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min( N, il ) || iu > N)
